battle.name: 癸酉之變
battle.brief: 一八一三年八月，河南滑縣的天理教起事席捲河南、山東、直隸三省。九月十五日夜，數十名起義者突入北京紫禁城，與內務府護軍激戰於隆宗門一帶，終被殲滅。英式燧發步槍當時僅少量經廣州口岸流入，綠營與團練手上的抬槍、鳥槍才是主力；這場戰爭真正較量的，是火藥、鉛彈與糧秣的供應鏈。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 擊錘打火比火繩穩。線性列陣的射速和精度都靠它撐著。

countries: 大清一方是中央與直隸、山東、河南三省的官僚與軍隊聯成的聯盟。中樞由兵部、都察院、戶部調度兵餉，京師警衛歸內務府與步軍營分掌：內務府護軍專司皇城與內廷宿衛，步軍營分守九門與外城，綠營各鎮分駐地方。地方上，直隸總督那彥成節制直隸、山東、河南三省兵力，滑縣事發後被指失察而革職，由顏檢接任；河南方面的吳熊光與山東方面的督撫同受責問，吳熊光其後被調任或貶謫，記載略有出入。剿匪的骨幹是臨時徵集的團練與鄉勇：河南山東一帶州縣奉文設練，練總多為地方紳士與生員，練勇自備鳥槍、抬槍、長矛與大刀，府縣出錢糧供應。起義一方沒有國家，也沒有軍令系統，天理教（官方檔案多稱八卦教）以香會、吃齋與結拜維持組織：河南滑縣李文成以教首身份首義，山東曹州與直隸大名、廣平一帶的教眾隨之響應，另有一批教眾潛入京師，準備內應。雙方都沒有外國勢力直接介入這場內亂；值得注意的是英國燧發步槍在當時已能經廣州口岸少量流入，但只到兩廣與閩浙沿海的營伍及少數收藏者手中，並未成為這場戰爭的制式裝備。
countriesEn: The Qing side was a coalition of the central bureaucracy with the officials and troops of Zhili, Shandong and Henan. At the centre, the Ministry of War, the Censorate and the Ministry of Revenue handled the dispatch of men and money, while the defence of the capital was divided between the Imperial Household Department and the Capital Garrison: the Household banner guards were responsible for the Forbidden City and the inner court, the garrison divisions held the nine gates and the outer city, and the Green Standard units garrisoned the provinces. In the field the Viceroy of Zhili exercised command over the troops of the three provinces; after the rising began at Huaxian he was blamed for the failure of his intelligence and was dismissed, and Yan Jian took over. The Henan official Wu Xionguang and the governor of Shandong were likewise held to account, and Wu was afterwards transferred or demoted, though the records differ on the exact handling. The backbone of the suppression was the locally raised banner militia and the village braves: the prefectures and counties of Henan and Shandong were ordered to raise drill units, whose drill leaders were usually local gentry and students, and whose men brought their own fowling pieces, shoulder muskets, spears and sabres, with the prefectures and counties paying for their food and wages. The insurgents had no state and no command system. The Tiansli cult, called the Eight Trigrams cult in the official files, was held together by incense meetings, fasting communions and sworn brotherhood: Li Wencheng, the cult leader of Huaxian in Henan, raised the first revolt, followers in Caozhou in Shandong and in Daming and Guangping in Zhili rose in answer, and a further group of followers slipped into the capital to prepare an insurrection from within. No foreign power was directly involved in this civil strife. It is worth noting that British flintlock muskets could already reach China in small numbers through the Canton factories, but they stayed in the coastal garrisons of Guangdong and Fujian and with a few private owners, and they never became standard equipment in this war.
people: 人物方面，嘉慶帝是整件事的震央。癸酉年九月他正在熱河木蘭行圍，秋獵途中聞報京師遭襲，連夜馳返，數日後抵京，隨即下詔究辦值宿宿衛與地方督撫。皇城內廷一帶，妃嬪與年幼的皇子安居其中，起義者始終未能接近，她們的安全全賴內務府護軍與內大臣的應變。當夜迎戰者，主要是內務府護軍、內大臣與步軍營城上兵卒，另有巡捕五營在街巷搜索；事後數十名失職的太監、護軍與校尉被究辦，內務府與步軍營的人事因此大改。起義一方的主腦是河南滑縣教首李文成，他起義前以符水、治病聚眾，起事後據滑縣城與清軍相持數月，最後城破時與家屬自焚殉難，或說他突圍被殺，各說不一。曹州方面的教首姓名與事跡記載互有出入，不能盡信。潛入京師的那支隊伍有數十人，其首領有記作陳爽者，其餘姓名多不可考；被俘的二人成為清廷追查教門的線索。地方官方面，那彥成因三省剿匪不力被革職，顏檢接任後改用重兵圍城的辦法；州縣官員多在失察與通匪之間被究辦，練總與里正被要求具結保甲，連坐之風由此打開。
peopleEn: The central figure is the Jiaqing Emperor. In the ninth month of the guiyou year he was hunting at Mulan in Jehol; on the road he learned that the capital had been attacked, rode back by night, reached Peking several days later and at once issued edicts holding the night watch and the provincial governors to account. Inside the inner court of the Forbidden City the imperial consorts and the infant princes were sitting out the night, the insurgents never came near them, and their safety rested entirely on the Household banner guards and the household ministers who reacted in time. Those who met the attack that night were chiefly the Household banner guards, the household ministers and the garrison soldiers on the walls, with patrol detachments searching the streets behind them; afterwards dozens of negligent eunuchs, guards and cadets were brought to account, and the personnel of the Household Department and of the Capital Garrison were reshuffled. The chief of the insurgents was Li Wencheng, the cult leader of Huaxian in Henan, who had gathered followers with charms and by healing the sick before the revolt, and who held Huaxian city against the imperial troops for several months afterwards; when the city fell he died with his family in the fire, though some accounts say he was killed trying to break out, and the stories differ. The name of the cult leader in Caozhou and his deeds are inconsistently recorded and cannot be taken at face value. The party that slipped into the capital numbered several dozen, its leader is given as Chen Shuang in one account, and little else about the men can be recovered; the two taken alive became the thread by which the court traced the cult. Among the officials, the Viceroy of Zhili, Na Yancheng, was dismissed for failing to suppress the revolt in the three provinces, and Yan Jian succeeded him and adopted a method of heavy encirclement; county and prefectural officers were caught between the charge of failure to detect and the charge of complicity, while drill leaders and village headmen were made to file guarantees for the household registration system, and a climate of collective liability opened with it.
kits: 燧發槍在這場戰爭裡的位置相當邊際，值得說明清楚。中國自康熙、雍正年間已有英製燧發步槍經廣州十三行渠道少量流入，數量從來有限，多落在兩廣與閩浙沿海的營伍、督撫衙門與私人收藏者手上；一八一三年之前，英式燧發步槍在河南、山東、直隸三省的軍隊中幾乎沒有列裝。真正上手的是國產抬槍與鳥槍：抬槍槍身沉重，要架在肩上擊發，多用火繩，也有匠人改裝成燧發機件；鳥槍是獵槍改用的輕型前裝滑膛槍，膛線粗、射程近，裝填繁瑣。起義群眾手中槍械多出自民間私藏，數量零散，火藥自製而鉛彈重鑄，射手未經統一操練。起義方攻滑縣用雲梯、穴地與火藥爆破，守方用密集火器與滾木擂石；皇城之夜，進攻者只有數支短槍與冷兵器，既無攻城器械，也無攻破內城門的辦法。清軍方面，綠營槍兵仍以冷兵器為主，槍械比例低；團練的槍械雜亂，火藥仰賴北方硝土與長途運入的硫磺，鉛料自雲南會澤啟運，到河南往往已耗去數月，所以本地常以回收舊彈重澆、銅片包鐵代替。運輸上，糧車與火藥靠衛河、黃河水運加陸路車隊；九月華北秋雨連綿，道路泥濘，攻守都受制於糧秣。結論很清楚：這場戰爭的勝負不取決於擊錘，而取決於火藥、鉛彈與糧食的供應鏈。
kitsEn: The place of the flintlock musket in this war was distinctly marginal, and that is worth stating plainly. British flintlock muskets had reached China in small numbers through the Canton hong merchants from the Kangxi and Yongzheng reigns onwards, but the quantities were always limited and they ended up with the coastal garrisons of Guangdong and Fujian, with the offices of the viceroys, and with private collectors. Before 1813 there were practically no British flintlock muskets in the armies of Henan, Shandong and Zhili. What the soldiers actually held were Chinese shoulder muskets and fowling pieces. The shoulder musket was heavy, had to be rested on the shoulder to fire, and was mostly a matchlock, though some craftsmen fitted flint mechanisms to it; the fowling piece was a light fore-end-loading smoothbore converted from a hunting gun, with a coarse bore, short range and slow loading. The guns in the hands of the insurgents came out of private caches, were scattered in number, their powder was made at home and their bullets recast, and the shooters had never been drilled together. The insurgents attacked Huaxian with ladders, mines and powder, and the defenders answered with close volleys of firearms, rolling logs and stones. The night attack on the Forbidden City was attempted with a handful of short guns and cold weapons, with no siege equipment and no means of breaching the inner gate. On the Qing side the Green Standard still fought mainly with cold weapons, the proportion of guns being low; the drill units had a jumble of weapons, their powder depending on nitre from the north and on sulphur carried a long way inland, while lead had to travel from Huize in Yunnan and had often spent months on the road before reaching Henan, so local practice was to recast recovered old bullets and to substitute copper plate sheathed in iron. In transport, grain and powder moved by water on the Wei and Yellow rivers and by wagon on land; the autumn rains in northern China in the ninth month turned the roads to mud, and both attack and defence were throttled by supply. The conclusion is plain: this war was not decided by the hammer of a flintlock but by the supply chain of powder, bullets and grain.
tactics: 起義方的打法是典型的秘密結社式攻城。教眾平日分散在鄉間，以香會、吃齋與結拜聯絡，一旦事起便在夜裡集結，扮作行商、腳夫或香客進城，先用冷兵器襲擊守門的團練與差役，再以人數壓垮城內守備，奪門而入後打開城門迎接城外人馬。據城之後，防守靠築寨、掘壕與拒馬，兵員不足時以老弱上城助守。河南滑縣是首義之地，起義軍據城抵抗清軍達數月，並分兵襲擊周邊縣城、斷絕糧道，把戰線拉成廣泛的騷擾網。曹州與直隸的響應者則各自攻破若干州縣，遇清軍主力即散為游眾，藉地形與村寨游擊。九月十五日夜的皇城突襲是其中最險的一手：數十名起義者事先潛入京師，藏在內城附近街巷，待夜分從宣武門一帶突入，企圖循內廷方向直入，殺向皇帝與妃嬪所在。實際戰況與預想相去甚遠：內務府護軍與內大臣自內中出迎，步軍營封閉城門、街巷戒嚴，起義者雖一度深入至隆宗門一帶，卻既無攻門器械，又缺乏彈藥，於是在火把與槍聲中耗盡。天明之後，殘餘者或被殺或被俘，防守方逐門搜索全城數日。清軍的戰術則是典型的圍城打援：一面以重兵合圍滑縣，切斷糧水，一面在要道上設卡查驗往來，斷絕城內外消息；團練分駐各鄉，築寨自守，遇小股起義軍便以槍矛圍殲，遇大股則報官請兵。收復失地時多用夜襲奪寨、迫降、斷糧三管齊下，避免了硬攻城牆的傷亡。
tacticsEn: The method of the insurgents was the classic secret-society assault on a walled town. In normal times the followers were scattered across the countryside, kept in touch by incense meetings, fasting communions and sworn brotherhood; when the moment came they mustered at night, dressed as pedlars, porters or pilgrims, slipped into the city, first struck the drill guards and constables at the gates with cold weapons, then overwhelmed the garrison by sheer numbers, and once the gate was taken opened it to the men waiting outside. Established in a city they relied on stockades, ditches and chevaux-de-frise for their defence, and when their fighting men ran short they put old men and boys on the walls to help. Huaxian in Henan, the first place to rise, held out against the imperial troops for several months; the rebels struck at the surrounding counties, cut the food routes and turned the fighting into a wide harassment. In Caozhou and Zhili the followers who rose in answer took scattered county towns, and dissolved into the countryside as soon as a real imperial force came near, fighting as skirmishers from villages and stockades. The night of the fifteenth of the ninth month was the most dangerous card they played: several dozen men had entered the capital beforehand and lay hidden in the streets near the inner city, waiting for the hour of the watch to strike from the direction of Xuanwu Gate and drive straight through to the inner court where the emperor and the imperial consorts were. What actually happened bore little resemblance to the plan. The Household banner guards and the household ministers came out from within and met them; the Capital Garrison shut the gates and put the streets under curfew; the insurgents reached as far as the Longzong Gate area but had neither siege equipment nor ammunition, and they were spent in torchlight and gunfire. By morning the survivors had been killed or taken, and the defenders spent the following days searching the city gate by gate. The Qing method, by contrast, was the classic siege with interceptions: heavy forces ringed Huaxian to cut its food and water while checkpoints on the roads and passes checked travellers and severed all contact with the outside; the drill units were posted in the villages behind their own stockades, surrounded and destroyed small bands of rebels with gunfire and spear, and called for regular troops when faced with a serious rising. The recovery of lost ground relied on night attacks on stockades, on offering terms of surrender, and on cutting food supplies, avoiding the cost of storming the walls head-on.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間線：嘉慶十八年即一八一三年八月河南滑縣首義，其後教眾響應於山東曹州與直隸各府；九月十五日夜，即公曆一八一三年十月八日，起義者突襲紫禁城；十月滑縣城破，首義者李文成死於城破；其後曹州、直隸一帶據點相繼肅清，至嘉慶十九年即一八一四年初基本平定，前後約一年。皇城之夜，突進者人數各說不一，官方諭旨與後人記述多作五六十人，亦有記數十人者；交戰於隆宗門一帶，起義者除被殺者外僅數人被俘，其中二人被解送京師，姓名有記作陳爽、陳連者，說法不一。兵力：清廷先後調集直隸、山東、河南三省綠營馬步兵數千，另有團練鄉勇數萬，分散在數百處寨卡與城鎮；起義者無固定編制，攻城時可集數千，戰後官方以擒斬數萬計，並稱被裹挾者以數十萬計，這些都是官方諭旨的措辭，實際數字無法核實。行政代價：事後那彥成革職、顏檢接任直隸總督，河南、山東多名州縣官員被貶調或革職，京師內務府與步軍營一批值宿人員被究辦，並掀起大規模追查教門的案件。時間跨度方面，皇城事變到嘉慶帝自熱河返京只隔數日，追緝餘黨的工作一直持續到年底。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The chronology: in the eighth month of Jiaqing's eighteenth year, 1813, the rising began at Huaxian in Henan, and was answered in Caozhou in Shandong and in the prefectures of Zhili; on the night of the fifteenth of the ninth month, which was 8 October 1813 in the western calendar, the insurgents attacked the Forbidden City; in the tenth month Huaxian fell and the first leader Li Wencheng died in the ruins of the city; the strongholds in Caozhou and Zhili were then reduced one by one, and by the beginning of Jiaqing's nineteenth year, 1814, the rising was essentially suppressed, a span of about a year. On the numbers at the palace that night the accounts differ; the official edicts and later writers usually give fifty or sixty men, others say only a few dozen. The fighting ran around the Longzong Gate, and apart from those killed the insurgents lost only a few men taken alive, two of whom were sent to Peking, named as Chen Shuang and Chen Lian in one account, though the names are not certain. On strength: the court moved several thousand Green Standard horse and foot from Zhili, Shandong and Henan, with tens of thousands of drill guards and village braves distributed among several hundred stockades, checkpoints and walled towns. The insurgents had no regular establishment; several thousand could be brought together for an assault, and afterwards the official count claimed tens of thousands killed and taken, with hundreds of thousands said to have been dragged in unawares; these are the phrases of the imperial edicts, and the real numbers cannot be verified. On the administrative cost: Na Yancheng was dismissed and Yan Jian took over as Viceroy of Zhili, a number of prefectural and county officers in Henan and Shandong were demoted, transferred or dismissed, and a batch of Household and Capital Garrison men on night watch were called to account, which set off a large-scale pursuit of cult cases across the provinces. In time, only a few days separate the attack on the palace from the emperor's return from Jehol, and the hunt for the remnants went on to the end of the year.
cause: 起因要分三層說。第一層是長期的鎮壓與地下化：白蓮教一系在明清以來屢遭打壓，到嘉慶朝改以香會、吃齋、結拜等民間形式傳播，教首多由草莽人物、醫者與遊方僧道擔任，信眾以農民、礦工、流民與城鄉手藝人為主。乾隆末至嘉慶初的白蓮教起義被平定之後，教門並未消失，而是轉入更隱蔽的形態，組織與地方械鬥結合，形成所謂教匪與團練互相消耗的局面。第二層是災荒與流動：嘉慶十八年前後直隸、山東、河南一帶乾旱、水災相繼，糧價飛升，災民流徙，教門成為流民最易加入的團體，會眾因此迅速膨脹。第三層是直接導火線：滑縣教首李文成在地方清剿與教內糾紛中被迫提前舉事，起義一旦爆開，山東曹州與直隸各府教眾群起響應，而事前情報未能上達，京師對方滲入者竟無人察覺，這才是皇城之變的直接背景。史觀上要注意，清廷敘事把這類起義一律稱為邪教與匪患，講究剿滅；近年的教派史研究則強調其群眾性、災荒成因與地方社會的對抗結構。兩種敘事對同一批史料的取捨不同，這也是這場戰爭至今仍被重新評價的原因。
causeEn: The causes are best given in three layers. The first is a long history of suppression followed by underground survival: the White Lotus tradition had been beaten down again and again since the Ming, and by the Jiaqing reign it passed on in folk forms such as incense meetings, fasting communions and sworn brotherhood, with local notables, healers and itinerant monks and Taoists serving as cult leaders, and with farmers, miners, vagrants and urban craftsmen as the core of the membership. The White Lotus rising of the late Qianlong and early Jiaqing years had been suppressed, but the cult did not disappear: it went deeper underground, its organisation became entangled with local feuds, and the result was a state of affairs in which cult bandits and drill guards ground each other down. The second layer is famine and displacement: in the years around Jiaqing's eighteenth year, drought and flood struck Zhili, Shandong and Henan in turn, grain prices soared, and the cult was the easiest group for vagrants to join, so the membership swelled quickly. The third layer is the immediate spark: the cult leader at Huaxian, Li Wencheng, was driven into open revolt ahead of schedule by the local crackdown and by disputes inside the cult, and once the rising was under way the followers in Caozhou and the prefectures of Zhili rose in answer; word of it did not reach the authorities in time, and the men who had slipped into the capital went unnoticed, and that is the direct background to the attack on the palace. On interpretation, it matters that the Qing's own narrative called all such risings heterodox teaching and banditry and was written to justify eradication, whereas recent scholarship on religious sects emphasises the popular character of the movement, the role of famine and the confrontational structure of local society. The two narratives select differently from the same record, and that is why this war is still being reassessed.
impact: 影響可以分近遠兩層。近層是宮禁與地方治理的重整。皇城被突襲在制度上是一次難堪的失敗：內務府與步軍營的宿衛編制、夜巡方式與門禁手續被重新訂立，失職人員遭撤換，皇城各門的警衛與火器配置加強，後宮與內廷侍衛的選任與輪值也收緊。地方上，督撫因失察受連帶處分，剿匪成為州縣官員的第一考績，連帶引發嚴禁教門、嚴禁民間私藏火器與密集的連坐式查辦，民間因此氣氛緊張，地方官多以多報、嚴辦自保。遠層在兵制：經此一役，團練與鄉勇在河南山東直隸全面制度化，地方武裝化程度大增；二十多年後太平天國戰爭興起時，地方練勇反而成為清廷最難駕馭的力量，湘軍、淮軍正是從這套團練體制裡生長出來並最終坐大。武器層面同樣有後果：民間火器被嚴禁，農村火器水準長期落後；而軍方對洋槍的需求開始上升，廣州口岸的英製燧發步槍進口量在道光年間明顯增加，這條供應線到鴉片戰爭前已經存在，卻未能改變清軍整體的射擊水準。
impactEn: The effects work on two levels, near and far. In the near term the attempt on the palace was a humiliating institutional failure: the system of night watch, the way patrols were run and the procedure at the gates of the Household Department and of the Capital Garrison were all rewritten, negligent personnel were removed, the guarding and the disposition of firearms at the gates of the Forbidden City were tightened, and the selection and rotation of the inner-court guards were revised. In the provinces, the governors and viceroys were punished in succession for failure to detect, the suppression of the cult became the first duty to be weighed in the assessment of county magistrates, and this brought in its wake a severe ban on the sects, a severe ban on private firearms in the hands of the people, and a wave of collective-punishment investigations, so that the atmosphere in the country tightened and most local officers made a practice of reporting numbers high and dealing harshly. In the longer term there was a change in military organisation: after this rising, drill units and village braves were institutionalised throughout Henan, Shandong and Zhili, and the militarisation of the countryside went a long way. When the Taiping rebellion broke out a little more than two decades later, these local forces turned out to be the hardest for the court to control, and the Xiang and Huai armies grew out of this very system of drill militia before growing too strong for it. The weapon question had consequences too: firearms in private hands were banned, rural weapon standards fell behind for a long time, while the army's demand for imported guns rose, and the number of British flintlock muskets entering through the Canton factories increased noticeably during the Daoguang reign. That supply line already existed before the Opium War, yet it had not changed the general standard of Qing shooting.
result: 結果分軍事、政治與象徵三層。軍事上，清方在半年內平定：滑縣城破後，首義者李文成死於城破，曹州與直隸的響應據點被逐一攻破或迫降，餘部在嘉慶十九年初基本被殲滅或潰散，起義失敗。政治上，清廷贏得了這場對手，但代價是把直隸、山東、河南三省推入高壓的連坐與清查，督撫更替、官員被貶，教門轉入更深的地下，中央集權並未因此實質加強。象徵上，皇城之夜是清代宮禁史上最刺眼的一頁，此後清廷對宮門警衛與旗籍宿衛的整頓一直延續到道光朝，紫禁城曾被教匪攻入成為後世反覆援引的案例。更長遠的結果是，癸酉之變證明了兩個道理：一是秘密結社加上災荒的組合，在王朝中晚期仍有爆發力；二是靠團練平叛的辦法會把國家推向地方軍閥化的方向。這一點，要到太平天國之後才完全顯形。
resultEn: The result has military, political and symbolic layers. Militarily the rising was crushed within half a year: after Huaxian fell the first leader Li Wencheng died in the ruins, the strongholds at Caozhou and in Zhili were taken one by one or starved into surrender, and the remnants were destroyed or scattered by the beginning of 1814. Politically the court won the contest, but the price was to push Zhili, Shandong and Henan into a state of high-pressure collective investigation and purge, with viceroys replaced and officials demoted, and the cult driven further underground; the centralisation of the state did not in fact grow. Symbolically, that night at the palace is the most glaring page in the history of the Qing palace guards, and the reforms of the palace gates and of the banner watch that followed ran on into the Daoguang reign; the story of the Forbidden City having been entered by cult rebels became a stock example, cited again and again. In the longer run the rising demonstrated two things: that the combination of a secret sect with famine still had explosive force in the later middle period of the dynasty, and that suppressing rebellion with drill militia pushes the state towards the militarisation of the localities. That second point only became fully visible after the Taiping war.
